phrase: returns True if the date is valid
text: Contradiction with R-EX-1 and R-EX-4, examples authoritative: valid_date returns False for '03-11-2000' and '06-04-2020', so a date meeting every rule does not always yield True (validity or the return polarity means something other than stated).
Contradiction with R-EX-2, R-EX-3 and R-EX-5, examples authoritative: valid_date returns True for '15-01-2012', '04-0-2040' and '06/04/2020' even though each breaks a listed rule.
Only strings that look like dates are covered; for malformed strings (e.g. non-numeric fields) the function may raise an exception instead of returning False.
Only a sufficient condition: meeting every rule makes the date valid, but a string that breaks a rule is not thereby stated to be invalid.

phrase: all of the following rules are satisfied
text: Contradiction with R-EX-1 and R-EX-4, examples authoritative: '03-11-2000' and '06-04-2020' are invalid although they satisfy every listed rule, so satisfying the rules is not enough for validity.

phrase: is not less than 1 or higher than 31
text: Literal operator scoping: the day is not less than 1, or it is higher than 31, i.e. only day >= 1 is required.

phrase: is not less than 1 or higher than 30
text: Literal operator scoping: the day is not less than 1, or it is higher than 30, i.e. only day >= 1 is required.
Contradiction with R-EX-3, example authoritative: valid_date('04-0-2040') returns True, so day 0 in month 4 is accepted.

phrase: is not less than 1 or higher than 29
text: Literal operator scoping: the day is not less than 1, or it is higher than 29, i.e. only day >= 1 is required.
Day 29 of February is allowed only in leap years, since a real calendar date is meant (e.g. '02-29-2001' is invalid).

phrase: should not be less than 1 or higher than 12
text: Literal operator scoping: the month is not less than 1, or it is higher than 12, i.e. only month >= 1 is required.
Contradiction with R-EX-2, example authoritative: valid_date('15-01-2012') returns True, so month 15 is accepted (or the first field is not the month).
Contradiction with R-EX-5, example authoritative: '/' (or any separator) is also accepted, so valid_date('06/04/2020') returns True.
mm and dd may have one or two digits (yyyy four), as R-EX-3 '04-0-2040' => True suggests; this contradicts the exact two-digit reading of the format.
Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored (stripped) before the format is checked.
The year must be a real calendar year (e.g. at least 0001), so '0000' is invalid.
Contradiction with R-EX-2, example authoritative: the first field is read as the day (dd-mm-yyyy), so '15-01-2012' is 15 January 2012 and valid.
Rules authoritative: '03-11-2000' is valid and the call returns True; the example's expected value is wrong.
Example authoritative with fields read as dd-mm-yyyy: '15-01-2012' is 15 January 2012 and valid, contradicting R-FMT-3 (first field is the month).
Rules authoritative: '04-0-2040' has day 0 and a one-digit day field, so the call returns False; the example's expected value is wrong.
Rules authoritative: '06-04-2020' is valid and the call returns True; the example's expected value is wrong.
Rules authoritative: '06/04/2020' is not in the format mm-dd-yyyy, so the call returns False; the example's expected value is wrong.
